findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Probability/Process/Predictable.lean:59,71,126 are generic over `ι`. In the PR, `ℝ≥0`-specific steps appear only at lines 91 and 121–129 (`exists_nat_ge`, `(n : ℝ≥0)`). Tau Ceti already uses `Filtration ℕ` in many places (e.g. Azuma.lean:96, Convergence.lean:340).
findings.fix: Take `{ι} [LinearOrder ι] [OrderBot ι] (ℱ : Filtration ι mΩ)` and write `{⊥} ×ˢ A` with `MeasurableSet[ℱ ⊥] A`. Add only the assumption that `generateFrom`, the integral-separation lemma and density need, e.g. `[(atTop : Filter ι).IsCountablyGenerated]` or a countable sequence of times tending to `atTop` in place of the `ℕ` cast. Then specialize to `ℝ≥0`.
findings.issue: `predictableRectangles`, `mem_predictableRectangles`, `measurableSet_of_mem_predictableRectangles` and `isPiSystem_predictableRectangles` are fixed to `Filtration ℝ≥0 mΩ` with `0`, but their proofs only use `bot_le` and `max`/`min`. Mathlib's `measurableSet_predictable_singleton_bot_prod` and `measurableSet_predictable_Ioc_prod` are stated for `[LinearOrder ι] [OrderBot ι]`.

findings.evidence: The density proof uses finiteness at two points: `measure_ne_top μ R` to build each indicator, and `(Lp.memLp f).integrable` to make `f` integrable. Both still work under the weaker assumption if you restrict to `Iic n ×ˢ univ`, since an L² function is integrable on a set of finite measure.
findings.fix: Assume `∀ t, μ (Iic t ×ˢ univ) ≠ ⊤` (or that every rectangle has finite measure). In the density proof, apply the integral-separation lemma to `f` restricted to `Iic n ×ˢ univ` for each `n`, then take the union over `n`. Keep the finite-measure case as a corollary.
findings.issue: `dense_span_indicatorConstLp_predictableRectangles` and `dense_span_indicatorConstLp_Ioc_prod` (line 183) assume `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]`. That excludes `dt ⊗ P` on `ℝ≥0 × Ω`, the measure for infinite-horizon Itô integrals, even though the module doc (line 23) says the result applies to Brownian time-product measures. The proof only needs each rectangle to have finite measure.

summary: The rectangle family, π-system and generation results are stated only for `ℝ≥0` time, although Mathlib's predictable API and these proofs work for a general linearly ordered time index with a least element. Density also assumes a finite measure, which excludes the infinite-horizon Brownian time-product measure that the docstring says the result is for.
